headline: AI demand lifts margins, guidance raised again
summary_short: Vertiv reported Q2 2026 net sales of $3,274.3M (+24.1% y/y) and diluted EPS of $1.27 (+53.0% y/y, adjusted diluted EPS $1.52, +60%), while adjusted operating margin expanded 410bp y/y to 22.6% on productivity and favorable price-cost.
summary_long: Net sales grew 24% y/y to $3,274.3M on 18% organic growth, a 5% acquisition contribution, and 1% FX tailwind; Americas led with 29% growth while EMEA was flat. Adjusted operating margin expanded 410bp y/y to 22.6% on operational execution, productivity, and favorable price-cost including tariff countermeasures. Diluted EPS rose 53% to $1.27 ($1.52 adjusted, +60%) on profit growth and a modestly higher share count. Adjusted free cash flow grew 234% y/y to $925M; cash rose to $2,810.6M from $1,728.4M at year-end, moving Vertiv to a net cash position with $5.6B liquidity. The company raised full-year 2026 guidance across net sales, adjusted operating profit/margin, adjusted diluted EPS, and adjusted free cash flow, and issued initial Q3 2026 guidance.

drivers.explanation: CEO Albertazzi and Chairman Cote attributed the quarter to sustained AI and general-compute demand, years of capacity investment, and strengthening global pipelines, giving management confidence to raise guidance.

Net sales grew on 18% organic growth, a 5% contribution from acquisitions, and a 1% favorable FX benefit; the release also flagged minor timing shifts from supply-chain congestion and multi-phased project execution as deployments scale.
Gross margin expanded to 37.7% from 34.0% y/y because cost of sales rose only 17.1% y/y against 24.1% revenue growth — the release does not discuss gross profit as a distinct line.

Operating profit rose $196M as adjusted operating margin expanded 410bp on operational execution, continued strong productivity, and favorable price-cost, inclusive of tariff impacts and associated countermeasures.
Mirrors the Operating income move above; both track the same y/y GAAP operating-profit growth reported in the release's earnings statement.

EBITDA growth follows the operating-profit increase above plus a higher depreciation and amortization addback ($39.4M + $76.4M in Q2 2026 vs $23.5M + $49.8M a year ago), consistent with continued capacity investment; not a labeled release metric.
Net income tracked operating-profit growth (+44% y/y) and lower net interest expense ($17.4M vs $21.3M), partly offset by higher income tax expense ($122.2M vs $96.9M) as pretax income rose 47% y/y.
EPS growth (+53% y/y) tracked net income growth; diluted share count rose slightly to 392.7M from 389.8M on option exercises, a modest drag not called out as a specific driver in the release.
Mirrors the Diluted EPS move above; both reflect the same net income growth against a comparable basic share count (384.6M vs 381.5M y/y).
